description: Grupo de estudiantes que viene a participar por puro corazón y diversión
summary: This project propose an interactive interface that allows the users (small local farmers) to access different agricultural variables of a defined parcel obtained via satellites so they can complement their existing knowledge to make decisions about crop rotation. This allows to a better farm production without the need of techincal abilities or high level education personel
details:
Sociological context

To delimit the users profile and produce an accurate tool the following sociodemographic variables were considered: geographic location, age, literacy level, and access to technological tools (internet connection and computers).

-Farmers profile

To characterize the profile of small agricultural producers and to construct this profile, we start from a general characterization of the sector at the provincial and departmental levels, using as primary sources the data from the 2018 National Agricultural Census (CNA) (processed by INTA-CONICET) and the demographic information from the 2022 National Census of Population, Households, and Dwellings (INDEC).

We define a Small Agricultural Producer (SAP) based on the following conceptual definition: "those who manage a farm holding (EAH) that meets the following conditions: the producer works directly on the holding; no permanent non-family paid workers are employed; it is not constituted under the legal form of a 'corporation' or 'partnership limited by shares'. The total area of the holding, in the Province of San Luis, is up to 1000ha (Obschatko et al., 2007:33).

-Geographic Location

The geographic scope focuses on the town of Luján, belonging to the Ayacucho Department in northern San Luis, using the " La Crisálida" Cooperative as its articulating axis. According to the 2022 National Census, the town has a total population of 2,559 inhabitants. According to various sources, it is characterized by having been a major orange fruit producer within San Luis, although this activity declined over time; in recent years, work has been done to recover that identity by incorporating new orange plantations as well as other citrus fruits.

It also features a local horticultural production matrix with various specializations, in this case, finding Pomology—the cultivation of fruits such as citrus, among others—and Olericulture, "which is the study and cultivation of edible herbaceous plants and vegetables, such as tomatoes, carrots, lettuce," etc.

Location defined: Luján, Ayacucho Department, Province of San Luis, with a focus on "La Crisálida" Cooperative

-Production Activity

Although published official statistics do not show an exact number of small producers residing exclusively in Luján, the provincial scale shows that the sector in San Luis registers a total of 2,376 small agricultural producers. It was also found that, according to the 2022 National Census of Population, Households, and Dwellings, there are 604 people employed in the branch of agriculture

-Age Group

Among Small Producers (SAP) Regarding the predominant age group among small producers, it is between 40 and 64 years old.

-Literacy Level

Out of the total producers surveyed in this dimension (2,281 cases), 2,232 people know how to read and write. However, 49 producers remain in a situation of illiteracy.

-Access to Technology

The survey on access to Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) also exposes a technological gap. Out of 2,353 small producers, regarding connectivity, 359 have internet access and 1,994 do not have internet access.

Developed tool

Based on the data obtained from NASA's archives like NASA POWER and The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem we developed a program that process light reflection data and weather information to obtain agricultural relevant indices like NDVI, EVI or MSI and precipitation data. This indicators are then translated to comprehensible common language (non technical) and shown to the user within an interactive interface.

The user should log their parcel information to personalize the data showed. It must include their name, parcel location, soil type, existing crop and wished crop for rotation.

This makes the tool easy to use and accesible to the farmer regardless of their educational level. It is also economical but useful compared to other tools (like drones) that requires technical knowledge and entail a monetary investment.

To make it more accesible, taking into account the common low literacy level expected, it's added a reading voice.

-Resources used

The following list shows the tools, coding languages, hardware and software used to develop the project:

  • Notebooks computers
  • Google Earth Engine API
  • Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem API
  • Visual Studio Code IDE
  • Python
  • Office Package
  • Gamma app
  • Figma
  • Various books, documents and papers

Prototype

The presented project it's a demo of the proposition so includes some interactive tools like sliding tabs that allows to visualize different setups.
